property_summary: If the caller had a nonzero balance before depositing, then after calling addToBalance their stored balance is strictly greater than their previous balance (i.e., the deposit does not reset a prior positive balance to a smaller value).

For any caller and any value, calling addToBalance() increases that caller's recorded userBalance by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., userBalance[caller] after the call == previous userBalance[caller] + msg.value); the mutant that zeroes the balance before adding breaks this rule for callers who already had a non-zero balance.

For any actor and any deposit amount, after calling addToBalance() the total balance recorded for any other arbitrary key k is unchanged by that call; the mutant that zeroes msg.sender's balance before adding can change balances at other keys when actor == k, violating this invariant for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller A and any deposit amount v, calling addToBalance() will not decrease the balance of any arbitrary address k (i.e., for all k, c.getBalance(k) after the call is >= c.getBalance(k) before the call); the mutant that zeroes msg.sender before adding can decrease balances (for k==msg.sender) so it violates this rule for some fuzzed inputs.

For any two distinct addresses depositor and probe and any deposit amount, calling addToBalance() from depositor does not change probe's stored balance; the mutant that zeroes msg.sender breaks this when depositor == probe (i.e., some fuzzed inputs where depositor equals probe will cause the mutant to set the depositor's balance to msg.value instead of adding, thus changing probe's balance), so the reference preserves probe's balance for all inputs while the mutant can change it for some.

For any caller A and any deposit v, calling addToBalance() preserves the balance of every OTHER address k != A (i.e., only the caller's own balance may change); the mutant that zeroes msg.sender before adding can change balances of other addresses when the caller equals that other address (i.e., when fuzz finds k == caller) — so the reference always leaves balances of all other addresses unchanged, while the mutant can violate this for some inputs.

property_summary: Calling addToBalance with value v never decreases the caller's stored balance (new balance >= old balance).

For any caller and any msg.value, calling addToBalance preserves that the contract's stored balance for that caller is at least as large as it was before the call (i.e., no balance decreases due to the operation); the mutant removing the require can allow wraparound so the stored balance can become smaller for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, calling addToBalance never decreases that caller's recorded balance (i.e., postBalance >= preBalance); removing the require allows overflow/wraparound so some deposits can make the stored balance smaller, violating this invariant.

For any depositor and any deposit amount less than 2**256 - preBalance, after addToBalance the stored balance equals preBalance + amount (no wraparound); the mutant (which omits the require) can overflow and make the stored balance differ (wrap to a smaller value) for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit amount, if the depositor's pre-call balance is less than 2**256 - amount (i.e., addition cannot overflow), then after addToBalance the stored balance equals preBalance + amount; the mutant (which removes the require) can violate this when addition would overflow.

For every caller and deposit amount, if the caller's pre-call balance is <= type(uint256).max - amount (so addition cannot wrap), then after addToBalance the stored balance equals preBalance + amount; the mutant removes the guard and thus can overflow causing a different stored balance for some fuzzed inputs.

getBalance(u) equals the observable contract balance change for u (i.e., balance deposited minus withdrawn) — specifically, after depositing an amount for an address, getBalance(addr) returns exactly the deposited amount (no off-by-one).
Calling addToBalance with value X does not change the contract balance or the caller's recorded balance unless X>0 (i.e., adding zero leaves balances unchanged and does not revert).
